name: Βk-2C-B
toxicities: Recreational toxicity and long-term health effects have not been studied, and the exact toxic dose is unknown.
effectsSummary: The archive describes beta-k-2C-B as a novel psychedelic with almost no human-use history and very limited pharmacology, metabolism and toxicity information.
dosageRemark: Archived oral table: threshold 50 mg; light 60-80 mg; moderate 80-100 mg; strong 100-150 mg; heavy 150 mg+; total 8-12 h, onset 20-70 min. User/resource educational information, not a recommendation. The page says recreational toxicity and long-term health effects have not been studied and exact toxic dose is unknown. lightMin corrected from threshold to source light lower bound.
generalRisks: No negative health effects have been clearly attributed in the infrequent low-to-moderate anecdotal reports, but the conclusions are uncertain and the toxicity is unstudied.
saferUse: Caution and harm reduction are recommended, because the history of human use is short and the toxicity is unstudied; occasional low and moderate reports are not safety evidence.
summary: βk-2C-B (bk-2C-B) is a psychedelic phenethylamine in the 2C family and the β-keto derivative of 2C-B. It was first described in scientific literature in 2004 and was identified as a designer drug in Europe in 2013.
